h: A house with a tale to tell
p: Hanbury Hall was built in the early 1700s for Thomas Vernon, a successful lawyer, and its red-brick, symmetrical front is a classic of its era. It is the kind of house that looks like a child's drawing of a stately home, in the best possible way, and it photographs beautifully from the end of the drive.

Those Thornhill paintings on the staircase are worth a slow look. Thornhill was a big name in his day, also known for his work at St Paul's Cathedral and Greenwich, so it is a bit of a coup to see his work in a Worcestershire country house. Spot the characters, look for the hidden messages and see which bits make you smile.

Outside, keep an eye out for the orangery and the bowling green, both nods to how the gentry liked to spend their leisure hours. The parkland beyond is ideal for a leg-stretch, with wide views and plenty of space for kids to run off steam. Dogs are often welcome in the parkland, so check the current rules on the day if yours is coming along.

Allow half a day if you want to take in both house and gardens without rushing. The surrounding lanes are pretty Worcestershire countryside, and Worcester itself, with its cathedral by the River Severn, is a short drive away if you fancy making a full day of it. Back in Droitwich Spa, the town's salty past is still a talking point, and a wander through the centre makes for a gentle end to the day.
